title: Petroleum Laboratory Specialist (Petro Lab SPC)
raw_text:
10-92L. MOS 92L--Petroleum Laboratory Specialist (Petro Lab SPC), CMF 92 (Eff 202510)
    a. Major duties. The laboratory petroleum specialist collects, tests, and analyze petroleum products to ensure quality
and compliance. Operate and maintain specialized laboratory equipment, accurately interpreting test results. Report
findings to commanders, providing expert advice on fuel management. Maintain laboratory standards, adhering to strict
quality control procedures. Troubleshoot equipment issues and manage laboratory resources, supporting operational
readiness. Duties for MOS 92L at each level of skill are:
        (1) MOSC 92L1O. Collect and test petroleum, oil, and lubricant (POL) samples for quality control, following
established procedures. Perform basic laboratory tests, measuring properties like viscosity, flash point, and water content.
Record test results accurately and maintain laboratory logs. Assist in operating and maintaining laboratory equipment,
ensuring proper calibration and functionality. Clean and organize the laboratory workspace, adhering to safety regulations.
Prepare samples for shipment to higher-level testing facilities. Follow instructions from supervisors and senior specialists
during testing procedures.
        (2) MOSC 92L2O. Perform a range of petroleum quality control tests, analyze samples for contaminants and
degradation. Operate and maintain complex laboratory equipment, troubleshoot malfunctions and perform preventative
maintenance. Interpret test results and identify potential fuel quality issues, recommend corrective actions. Prepare
detailed reports on laboratory findings, document test procedures and results. Supervise and train junior petroleum
laboratory specialists, ensure adherence to safety protocols. Calibrate and standardize laboratory equipment, maintain
accuracy and reliability. Assist in developing and implementing quality control procedures, improving testing efficiency.
Manage laboratory inventory, ordering supplies and maintaining stock levels.
        (3) MOCS 92L converts to 92F3O.
    b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. The petroleum laboratory specialist must
possess the following qualifications:
        (1) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
        (2) A physical profile of 211221.
        (3) Normal color vision.
        (4) Qualifying scores.
            (a) A minimum score of 91 in aptitude area ST.
            (b) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350 cm,
Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in Physical Demand Category in
“Moderate” (Gold).
        (5) Mandatory formal training. Completion of MOS 92L course conducted under the auspices of the U.S. Army
Quartermaster School; or meet the ACASP criteria listed in AR 601-210. Waiver requests can be submitted to the Office
of the Quartermaster Commandant Enlisted Proponent Office at USARMY Ft Lee, VA, 23801. TRADOC List QM Enlisted
Personnel Development usarmy.lee.tradoc.list.qm-enlisted-personnel-development@army.mil.
    c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all enlisted MOS)).
        (1) D6--Operational Data Analyst (personnel only)
    d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill level are listed in
the following tables:
        (1) Table 10-92L-1. Physical requirements.
        (2) Table 10-92L-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
        (3) Table 10-92L-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
